messages.author: a225fe7bebd5f312
messages.subject: Multilevel Fit Statistics
parts:
Hi,

Kudos to Yves and the team for including multilevel SEM in the newest version of lavaan! Having gotten this far, I wonder if I can persuade the developers to a bit further to include level-specific fit statistics in the output. (And yes, I know that within and between versions of SRMR are included.) Hox (2002, 2010) was among the first to identify problems with including information from both levels in the usual fit stats (e..g, chi-square, RMSEA, CLI, TLI) and Ryu and West (2009—see also Ryu, 2014) offered solutions that I think are fairly easy to implement. (See Janis et al., 2016) for an implementation example.) Their solution is to create partially saturated models for the test level in question. Consider a 4-item CFA, with each item loading on a latent factor at each level. The PS_B model specifies the covariance matrix at the within level and the hypothesized model at the between level; the PS_W model flips that script. These models are compared to fully saturated models (covariances at both levels), the logic being that the chi-square for the partially saturated model includes information only for the level in question. For example, the PS_B model identifies the extent to which the between model contributes to the fit information. Using the partially saturated models (and corresponding independence models) provides information for computing level-specific fit statistics, including CLI, TLI, and RMSEA.

Now it’s not terribly hard to write a function to pull the requisite information from all of the models (I’ve done it) but it would be a boon to those of use who study collectives (e.g., groups) to build those fit estimates into lavaan. Thanks to Yves and the team for considering my request.

Best,

Joe
